context: Coinbase's XRP-backed USDC loans connect XRP custody, cbXRP on Base, Morpho lending markets and Circle-issued USDC. The relationship is economically material but not a direct XRP spot-demand measure.
decisions: Represent XRP underlying, Coinbase cbXRP reserve, cbXRP Base supply, cbXRP DEX liquidity, Morpho collateral, USDC debt, vault supply, liquidations and native XRP spot flows as separate entities/series.

Classify the 62.5% cbXRP/USDC Morpho market as a strongly supported likely Coinbase product market, not an officially confirmed exclusive Coinbase market. Preserve permissionless access and unknown Coinbase channel share.
Treat the $59.11M borrow and $148.9M collateral snapshot as market-wide public API observations, not Coinbase customer balances or Circle-provided capital.
Treat Circle as the issuer of the USDC debt asset on Base and XRPL; do not classify Circle as lender, vault supplier or cross-chain bridge operator without address-level evidence.
Treat liquidations as cbXRP collateral transfers first. Do not convert collateral seized into native XRP selling pressure without a traced redemption/unwrap and subsequent market sale.
Keep market utilization, vault concentration, LLTV, Chainlink oracle parameters, liquidation count, debt repaid and collateral-at-risk as risk-context candidates, not admitted price predictors.
Preserve the Morpho app/aggregator liquidity discrepancy and Coinbase/Morpho liquidation-penalty discrepancy as explicit data-quality blockers.
invariants: Underlying XRP backing cbXRP is not the same asset as cbXRP collateral on Base.
Coinbase states wrapped-asset backing is held 1:1 and not sold, transferred or used for another purpose; this is a company statement, not an independent audit.
Coinbase interface activity is not equivalent to all permissionless Morpho market activity.
USDC issuance by Circle is not proof Circle supplied the loan market.
Market-wide collateral at risk is not expected liquidation, loss, net external capital or XRP spot sell volume.
Do not admit any new market feature before synchronized point-in-time data, provenance, independent corroboration, leakage controls, walk-forward baselines, calibration and shadow evaluation.
